title: Why does AI make things up? AI hallucination explained
caption:
ChatGPT made up 6 court cases, and lawyers filed them in federal court. Why does AI make things up? It's called AI hallucination.
It even said it had double-checked. Why? AI gets graded like a test where "I don't know" scores zero.
Has a chatbot ever made something up to you?
keywords: why does AI make things up
pinned_comment: The fake case even listed 3 real judges as its panel. One of them doesn't sit on that court at all. Has a chatbot ever invented a source on you?

sounds.name: Kind 1: a calm lo-fi or chill-beats instrumental from Sounds > Trending (US), no vocals
sounds.why: Soft, steady and wordless, so it sits under a fast narrator without fighting it; it suits the court-documents-on-paper look.

sounds.name: Kind 2: a low, suspenseful true-crime or mystery-documentary bed (slow pulse, light piano or synth pads), no vocals
sounds.why: The first half plays like a courtroom story (fake case, double-check, NO SUCH CASE stamp, $5,000 fine); a quiet tension bed keeps people to the payoff.

sounds.name: Kind 3: a curious, light 'explainer' pluck or pizzicato loop, no vocals
sounds.why: Fits the second half (guessing, the multiple-choice test, the old SAT) and the channel's calm, curious tone; it loops cleanly with the film.
